# SankeyChart

## Overview

`SankeyChart` is the top-level compound chart component that composes `ChartHeader`, `ChartLegend`, `DataDisplay`, `SankeyGroup`, and `ChartFooter` into a complete Sankey-flow visualization. All design tokens come from the CSS cascade — DataVis palette tokens (`--DataVis-Categorical-Bold-{n}`) via `generateDataVisCSS` → `useStyleInjection`, and surface/typography tokens via `useBrandCSSNew` — both injected at `@layer brand`. No runtime JS token resolver; no hardcoded dimensions, colours, typography, or spacing.

The chart accepts canonical `FlowDataPoint[]` where each row is `{source, target, value}` (legacy `ChartSeriesDataPoint[]` — `category`=source, `series`=target — is still accepted). Unique node names are derived automatically from the union of sources and targets — the default legend auto-generates one chip per node.

## Figma Reference

- **Node ID**: `967:125109`
- **Design File**: DataVis-Components
- **Figma URL**: https://www.figma.com/design/uA5ExvS0cNXbDEKzT9Rnrt/DataVis-Components?node-id=967-125109

## Architecture

```
SankeyChart
└── ChartAccessibility (role="figure", summary, hidden data table, aria-live region)
    └── div (flex column, gap = var(--SankeyChart-gap, var(--Spacing-5)))
        ├── ChartHeader (optional, default true) — ChartTitle + ChartSubtitle
        ├── ChartLegend (optional, default false) — one ChartKey per unique node
        ├── DataDisplay (optional, default false) — label + value + semantic badge
        │   • Static mode: values from dataDisplayConfig
        │   • Hover mode:  values update live on node/link hover
        ├── div (flex: 1, minHeight: 0) — SankeyGroup wrapper
        │   └── SankeyGroup
        │       • d3-sankey layout
        │       • top category labels (optional)
        │       • left/right DataHead columns (optional)
        │       • hover badge (optional)
        │       • own ChartAccessibility wrapper for the atomic group
        └── ChartFooter (optional, default true) — annotationLeft + annotationRight
```

## Import

```tsx
import SankeyChart from "./charts/SankeyChart";
import type {
  SankeyChartProps,
  SankeyGroupConfig,
  SankeyChartLegendConfig,
  SankeyDataDisplayConfig,
  SankeyNodeHoverData,
  SankeyLinkHoverData,
} from "./charts/SankeyChart";
```

## Data Format

```typescript
import type { FlowDataPoint } from "./types/chart-data";

const data: FlowDataPoint[] = [
  { id: "1", source: "Search", target: "Organic", value: 420 },
  { id: "2", source: "Search", target: "Paid", value: 180 },
  { id: "3", source: "Social", target: "Organic", value: 210 },
  { id: "4", source: "Social", target: "Paid", value: 140 },
  { id: "5", source: "Organic", target: "Signup", value: 380 },
  { id: "6", source: "Organic", target: "Bounce", value: 250 },
  { id: "7", source: "Paid", target: "Signup", value: 220 },
  { id: "8", source: "Paid", target: "Bounce", value: 100 },
];
```

Conventions:

- **`source`** — the source node name.
- **`target`** — the target node name.
- **`value`** — the flow magnitude (positive number).
- **`color`** _(optional)_ — per-edge link colour override; also inherited by the first encountered endpoint for legend fallback.
- Nodes appearing as both `source` and `target` are automatically placed into an intermediate stage by `d3-sankey`.

**Legacy format**: `ChartSeriesDataPoint[]` is still accepted — `category`=source, `series`=target, `value`=flow magnitude — for backward compatibility. New code should prefer `FlowDataPoint[]` above.

See `docs/DATA-FORMAT.md` for the full canonical data specification.

## Props Interface (Organized Props Pattern)

```typescript
interface SankeyChartProps {
  // Parent component props
  data: FlowDataPoint[] | ChartSeriesDataPoint[];
  width?: number | string; // default 432
  height?: number | string; // default 400
  fullWidth?: boolean; // default false — stretch to 100% width
  chartHeader?: boolean; // default true
  chartLegend?: boolean; // default false
  dataDisplay?: boolean; // default false
  chartFooter?: boolean; // default true
  interactive?: boolean; // default true
  animated?: boolean; // default false
  hoverBadge?: boolean; // default false

  // Child component configurations
  chartHeaderConfig?: ChartHeaderConfig;
  chartLegendConfig?: ChartLegendConfig;
  dataDisplayConfig?: DataDisplayConfig;
  sankeyGroupConfig?: SankeyGroupConfig; // bundles every SankeyGroup option
  chartFooterConfig?: ChartFooterConfig;

  // Accessibility
  accessibility?: AccessibilityConfig;
}
```

### ChartHeader Config (`chartHeaderConfig`)

| Prop                 | Type      | Default | Description                |
| -------------------- | --------- | ------- | -------------------------- |
| `chartTitleValue`    | `string`  | -       | Chart title text           |
| `chartSubtitleValue` | `string`  | -       | Chart subtitle text        |
| `subtitle`           | `boolean` | `true`  | Show/hide the subtitle row |

### ChartLegend Config (`chartLegendConfig`)

| Prop    | Type                | Default        | Description                                                      |
| ------- | ------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items` | `ChartLegendItem[]` | auto-generated | Manual legend items; override auto-generation from unique nodes. |

Legend auto-generation:

1. If `items` are provided, they are used verbatim.
2. Otherwise one chip is generated per unique node name (union of `source` and `target`, or the legacy `category`/`series`) in first-appearance order.
3. Colour fallback: per-edge `color` (when present on the first occurrence of the node) → `var(--DataVis-Categorical-Bold-{i+1})` → undefined.

### DataDisplay Config (`dataDisplayConfig`)

See **[DataDisplay Integration](./DataDisplayIntegration.md)** for the full reference.

| Prop                    | Type                                                                       | Default    | Description                                                     |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mode`                  | `"static" \| "hover"`                                                      | `"static"` | Static uses provided values; hover updates on node/link hover   |
| `formatHoverLeadValue`  | `(hover: SankeyNodeHoverData \| SankeyLinkHoverData) => string`            | -          | Custom formatter for the main value in hover mode               |
| `formatHoverBadgeValue` | `(hover: SankeyNodeHoverData \| SankeyLinkHoverData, totalFlow) => string` | -          | Custom formatter for the badge value in hover mode              |
| `mainLabelValue`        | `string`                                                                   | -          | Main label above the data value                                 |
| `type`                  | `"Left" \| "Center"`                                                       | `"Left"`   | Layout variant                                                  |
| `dataHead`              | `DataHeadConfig`                                                           | -          | Full DataHead configuration (lead value, supporting data, etc.) |
| `badgeConfig`           | `BadgeConfig`                                                              | -          | Full badge configuration (value, etc.)                          |

Hover mode:

- When a **node** is hovered, `mainLabelValue` becomes the node name, `dataHead.dataLeadValue` the node flow value, and `badgeConfig.value` the node's percentage of total flow.
- When a **link** is hovered, `mainLabelValue` becomes `"source → target"`, `dataHead.dataLeadValue` the link value, and `badgeConfig.value` the link's percentage of total flow.
- Custom formatters receive the raw hover payload so consumers can render custom strings (e.g., currency with locale, % of sub-total, etc.).

## Usage Examples

### Basic Chart

```tsx
<SankeyChart
  data={[
    { source: "A", target: "X", value: 120 },
    { source: "A", target: "Y", value: 30 },
    { source: "B", target: "X", value: 90 },
    { source: "B", target: "Y", value: 80 },
    { source: "C", target: "Y", value: 60 },
  ]}
  chartHeaderConfig={{
    chartTitleValue: "Flow Analysis",
    chartSubtitleValue: "Traffic distribution across channels.",
  }}
/>
```

### Full Configuration

```tsx
<SankeyChart
  data={data}
  width={720}
  height={480}
  chartHeader={true}
  chartLegend={true}
  dataDisplay={true}
  chartFooter={true}
  interactive={true}
  animated={true}
  hoverBadge={true}
  chartHeaderConfig={{
    chartTitleValue: "User Journey",
    chartSubtitleValue: "Source → destination flow.",
  }}
  dataDisplayConfig={{
    mode: "hover",
    mainLabelValue: "Hover a node or link",
    dataHead: { dataLeadValue: "-", supportingData: false },
    badgeConfig: { value: "-" },
  }}
  sankeyGroupConfig={{
    topCategoryLabels: true,
    leftOutsideLabels: true,
    rightOutsideLabels: true,
    topCategoryLabelConfig: { labels: ["Source", "Midpoint", "Destination"] },
    link: { opacity: 0.3, colorBy: "source" },
    node: { nodeGap: 16, cornerRadius: 4 },
    hoverBadgeConfig: {
      formatNodeValue: (v, n) => `${n}: ${v.toLocaleString()}`,
      formatLinkValue: (v, s, t) => `${s} → ${t}: ${v.toLocaleString()}`,
    },
    onNodeClick: (d) => console.log("Node clicked:", d.name),
    onLinkClick: (d) => console.log("Link clicked:", d.source, "→", d.target),
  }}
  chartFooterConfig={{
    annotationLeftValue: "Source: Analytics.",
    annotationRightValue: "FY 2025-26.",
  }}
  accessibility={{
    enabled: true,
    dataTable: true,
    ariaLabel: "User journey sankey chart",
  }}
/>
// `animated={true}` kicks off a fully token-driven entry animation:
//   • Nodes fade in, staggered by column (`delay = node.depth * offsetDelay`).
//   • Connectors grow left-to-right via `stroke-dashoffset`, staggered by
//     source-node stage so each link grows alongside its source column.
// Once the entry cascade settles, any subsequent change to the `data` prop
// smoothly morphs the chart — existing nodes tween `y`, `height`, `opacity`,
// `fill`; connectors tween their `d`, `stroke-width`, and `stroke`; and
// outside labels (left + right DataHead columns) slide their `top` value
// in sync with their node's `y0` / `centerY` and fade in when their node
// is new. New nodes fade in + grow from zero height at the same time.
// Data-change timing uses the `transitionAnimation` token chain with NO
// stagger (all elements morph in parallel) so the re-layout feels cohesive
// and nothing snaps into place. Hover dimming continues to run at hover-
// token speed throughout. All timing values resolve from CSS custom properties.
// See SankeyGroup.md § Motion / Animation.
```

### Full Width

```tsx
<SankeyChart data={data} fullWidth />
```

## Design Tokens Used

| Property       | CSS Custom Property                   | Fallback           | Purpose                                                           |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Chart gap      | `--SankeyChart-gap`                   | `var(--Spacing-5)` | Outer column gap (header → legend → DataDisplay → group → footer) |
| Legend colours | `--DataVis-Categorical-Bold-{1..5}` | —                  | Default node palette (fallback when `data[i].color` is absent)    |

> All design tokens come from the CSS cascade. DataVis palette tokens are injected via `generateDataVisCSS` → `useStyleInjection`, and surface/typography tokens via `useBrandCSSNew`, both at `@layer brand`.

## Flow Layout

Stages are inferred automatically by `d3-sankey` from the source/target topology:

- A node that only appears as a `source` (or legacy `category`) is a **source** (leftmost stage).
- A node that only appears as a `target` (or legacy `series`) is a **sink** (rightmost stage).
- A node appearing as both is an **intermediate** stage between its incoming and outgoing edges.

Stage count, node positions, and link curves are computed every render from `data`; no manual stage indices are required.

## Outside Labels

When `leftOutsideLabels` / `rightOutsideLabels` are enabled on `sankeyGroupConfig`, one `DataHead` is rendered per border-column node:

- **Left column** — one DataHead per source node, labels right-aligned so they abut the sankey node edge.
- **Right column** — one DataHead per sink node, labels left-aligned so they abut the sankey node edge.
- Column widths **auto-size** to the longest label in the column (measured via the Canvas API).
- Vertical anchor is controlled by `labelAlignment`: `"top"` (default, matches Figma spec — top edge aligns with the node's top edge) or `"center"` (vertically centered on the node band).

Customisation is available via `leftOutsideLabelConfig` and `rightOutsideLabelConfig`:

```tsx
sankeyGroupConfig={{
  leftOutsideLabels: true,
  leftOutsideLabelConfig: {
    size: "S",
    labelAlignment: "top",
    valueFormat: { type: "number", abbreviate: true },
    showSupportingLabel: true,
    supportingLabel: (name) => `Source: ${name}`,
  },
}}
```

## Top Category Labels

Enabling `topCategoryLabels` on `sankeyGroupConfig` renders one label per stage above the chart:

- **First stage** label is **left-aligned** to its column's leading edge (`x0`).
- **Last stage** label is **right-aligned** to its column's trailing edge (`x1`, via `translateX(-100%)`).
- **Middle stages** are **centered** on their column midpoint.

Override labels via `topCategoryLabelConfig`:

```tsx
sankeyGroupConfig={{
  topCategoryLabels: true,
  topCategoryLabelConfig: {
    labels: ["Source", "Midpoint", "Destination"],
    // or a resolver:
    // labels: (stageIndex, nodesInStage) => `Stage ${stageIndex + 1}`,
  },
}}
```

## Hover Interaction

With `interactive={true}` (the default), hovering a node or link:

1. Fires the relevant `onNodeHover` / `onLinkHover` callback with a typed payload.
2. Dims non-hovered links and keeps the hovered one at full opacity.
3. Emits an ARIA live-region announcement via `useChartAccessibility` (which composes `useAriaLiveRegion` internally) so screen-reader users hear the active node/link.
4. Optionally updates DataDisplay values (when `dataDisplayConfig.mode === "hover"`) so the KPI reflects the hovered element.
5. Optionally renders a cursor-following `HoverBadge` (when `hoverBadge={true}`).

### Hover Badge

```tsx
<SankeyChart
  data={data}
  interactive
  hoverBadge
  sankeyGroupConfig={{
    hoverBadgeConfig: {
      formatNodeValue: (value, name) => `${name}: ${value.toLocaleString()}`,
      formatLinkValue: (value, source, target) =>
        `${source} → ${target}: ${value.toLocaleString()}`,
    },
  }}
/>
```

The hover badge uses motion tokens for its enter/exit animation and inverts `colourMode` for visibility contrast.

## DataDisplay Hover Mode

With `dataDisplayConfig.mode: "hover"`, the DataDisplay block becomes live-updating:

- On **node hover** the DataDisplay shows the node name + its total flow through the sankey.
- On **link hover** it shows `source → target` + the link's flow value.
- The semantic badge reflects the percentage of total flow by default, or a custom value from `formatHoverBadgeValue(hover, totalFlow)`.

The DataDisplay is cross-linked to the SankeyGroup via `ariaControlsId` (DataDisplay's `id` is passed as SankeyGroup's `ariaControlsId`) so assistive tech treats the KPI and the chart as a unit.

## Responsiveness

- Numeric `width`/`height` are emitted as `px` values on the outer container.
- String values (`"100%"`, `"50vh"`, etc.) propagate through the `ChartAccessibility` wrapper via `containerStyle`, so percentage values can resolve through the DOM tree.
- When `fullWidth={true}`, the chart container is set to `width: 100%` and `SankeyGroup` is handed `fullWidth={true}` so its internal `ResizeObserver` drives the d3-sankey layout.
- The SankeyGroup is wrapped in a `flex: 1, minHeight: 0` div so it fills the chart's remaining vertical space regardless of how much room the header, legend, DataDisplay, and footer take.

## Accessibility

`SankeyChart` ships the full reusable ARIA accessibility stack out of the box. The chart-level wrapper is produced by `ChartAccessibility` with `chartType="sankey"`, driven by the `useChartAccessibility` hook, and the inner `SankeyGroup` is automatically opted out of its own wrapper (`accessibility={{ enabled: false }}`) to avoid a nested `role="figure"`.

### Reusable layers

| Layer                                       | Component / Hook                              | Enabled by                | Turn off by                                         |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `role="figure"` + `aria-label`              | `ChartAccessibility`                          | default                   | `accessibility.enabled: false`                      |
| Auto-generated natural-language summary     | `ChartAccessibility` (`chartType="sankey"`)   | default                   | `accessibility.summary: "custom string"` (override) |
| Hidden data table (rows = flow edges)       | `ChartAccessibility`                          | default                   | `accessibility.dataTable: false`                    |
| Debounced `aria-live` region on hover/focus | `useChartAccessibility` + `useAriaLiveRegion` | default                   | n/a — always on while the chart is interactive      |
| Custom `aria-label` override                | `ChartAccessibility`                          | `accessibility.ariaLabel` | omit the field                                      |
| Roving tab index across nodes               | `useRovingTabIndex` (inside `SankeyGroup`)    | `interactive: true`       | `interactive: false`                                |
| `aria-controls` linking Group → DataDisplay | `SankeyChart` wiring (`dataDisplayId`)        | `dataDisplay: true`       | `dataDisplay: false`                                |
| Decorative `aria-hidden` on SVG elements    | `SankeyGroup`                                 | always                    | n/a                                                 |

### Example screen-reader output

> _"sankey diagram titled 'Flow Analysis'. Shows flows between 5 nodes from 3 sources to 2 targets, totaling 380. Highest value: 120 at A (X)."_

And when the user arrow-keys onto a node:

> _"Oil, 60, stage 1"_

### Custom summary and hidden-table control

```tsx
<SankeyChart
  data={flowData}
  chartHeaderConfig={{ chartTitleValue: "Energy Flow" }}
  accessibility={{
    summary: "Q4 energy flow. Solar doubled year-over-year while coal fell 30%.",
    dataTable: false, // suppress the hidden <table> if you don't want SR row navigation
    ariaLabel: "Q4 energy flow sankey diagram",
  }}
/>
```

### Fully disable the wrapper

```tsx
<SankeyChart data={data} accessibility={{ enabled: false }} />
// The SankeyGroup's own wrapper is still opt'd out because the Chart always
// passes { enabled: false } downwards — so the tree renders with no role="figure".
```

### Why the delegation matters

`SankeyGroup` carries its own `<ChartAccessibility>` wrapper for **standalone use**. Inside `SankeyChart` the parent owns the wrapper, so the Chart automatically passes `accessibility={{ enabled: false }}` to the Group to avoid a nested `role="figure"`, duplicate hidden summary/table, and two `aria-live` regions racing on the same hover. You don't have to do anything — but if you compose `SankeyGroup` manually you should pass the same prop yourself.

See **[ChartAccessibility.md → Delegation Pattern](./ChartAccessibility.md)** and **[useChartAccessibility.md](./useChartAccessibility.md)** for the full a11y reference.

## Performance Notes

- `detectedNodeInfo`, `resolvedLegendItems`, and `totalFlow` memoize off `data` to avoid re-deriving node topology each render.
- `SankeyGroup` memoizes the D3 layout off its own inputs; animated renders are throttled via motion tokens.
- All design tokens resolve via CSS custom properties — zero runtime JS token resolution overhead.
